Do not explain away syncope

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 20-year-old reports two episodes of syncope during exercise. His resting ECG happens to show respiratory sinus arrhythmia. A relative died suddenly while playing sport. What is the best interpretation of the ECG finding in this context?

  1. A pacemaker is automatically required for sinus variation
  2. The sinus variation may be benign, but it does not explain or dismiss the exertional syncope
  3. Respiratory sinus arrhythmia proves all syncope is harmless
  4. The sinus variation itself establishes atrial fibrillation
  5. Anticoagulation is indicated solely for the breathing-related variation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

The sinus variation may be benign, but it does not explain or dismiss the exertional syncope

Concerning symptoms and family history warrant evaluation independently of an incidental normal rhythm variant.

Understanding the options

The sinus variation may be benign, but it does not explain or dismiss the exertional syncope
Concerning symptoms and family history warrant evaluation independently of an incidental normal rhythm variant.
Respiratory sinus arrhythmia proves all syncope is harmless
A normal variant cannot exclude another important cause.
The sinus variation itself establishes atrial fibrillation
The rhythms have different ECG characteristics.
Anticoagulation is indicated solely for the breathing-related variation
This normal variant is not an anticoagulation indication.
A pacemaker is automatically required for sinus variation
Pacing requires an appropriate clinical rhythm indication, not this finding alone.
